purpose: Declare the external, non-owning current-events sources, viewing lenses, time horizons and geographic-mentions projection used by the public Current World surface. Feed presence, repetition and mapped mentions do not make a claim true, important or part of project canon.

sorting.rule: The article river is ordered mechanically by publication time after URL de-duplication. The project does not assign partisan, ideological, truth, importance or source-quality scores.
sorting.coverage_clusters: Repeated-coverage clusters are formed from headline-token overlap across distinct source domains. They describe repeated coverage only and are not an importance, consensus or truth score.

providers.name: GDELT DOC 2.0
providers.provenance: Article titles, publication times, source domains, source-country metadata and links are supplied by GDELT's index of external publishers.
providers.boundary: GDELT is a discovery/index layer. The linked publisher remains the source for the article; source-country metadata describes the publisher/source context and must not be presented as the event location.

providers.name: Hacker News Firebase API
providers.role: Technology and computing community link stream
providers.provenance: Titles, timestamps and outbound URLs are community-submitted Hacker News items.
providers.boundary: A Hacker News item is a community link, not independent journalistic verification.

providers.name: Spaceflight News API
providers.provenance: The API aggregates article metadata from spaceflight publishers and links to the original story.
providers.boundary: The aggregator is a discovery layer; claims should be evaluated at the linked publisher.

geo.boundary: The spatial pulse maps locations mentioned near the active search terms in monitored coverage. It is a geography-of-mentions view, not verified event geolocation, casualty mapping, territorial adjudication or a measure of real-world importance.

epistemic_boundary: Presence in a live feed establishes only that an external source or community item was indexed. Similar headlines establish repeated coverage, not corroboration. Geographic mentions establish media-location context, not that the mapped place is where an event occurred.
